articles.headline: Adif inicia la recepción de la intermodal de Lugo, aún sin fecha de apertura
articles.subtitle: El Administrador Ferroviario confirmó el martes que tramita la recepción de la obra, pero no concreta cuándo entrará en servicio ni cuándo se reabrirá al tráfico la Rúa Conde de Fontao, cerrada desde abril.
articles.body:
Adif confirmó este martes que ha iniciado el trámite de recepción de la obra de la estación intermodal de Lugo, aunque sin concretar fecha de puesta en servicio. El organismo respondía así al debate abierto la semana pasada, cuando la alcaldesa, Elena Candia, pidió una reunión con su presidente para abordar el proyecto que unirá la estación con la Ronda da Muralla mediante un ascensor y una rampa mecanizada, financiado con fondos Novo Norte.

La regidora solicitó además una recepción parcial que permita reabrir al tráfico la Rúa Conde de Fontao, cortada desde finales de abril pese a estar aparentemente terminada desde principios de verano. Adif replica que esas obras forman parte de un contrato conjunto —el edificio de viajeros, el paso inferior peatonal, la plaza urbana, el parque del Sagrado Corazón y los andenes— y que la recepción debe realizarse sobre el conjunto. El organismo ya ha solicitado la recepción completa, en fase de tramitación.

La demora podría deberse al periodo vacacional, aunque no se descartan motivos políticos: el ministro Óscar Puente anunció en junio una visita para inaugurar la terminal, antes de la moción de censura en Lugo. Mientras tanto, Renfe reorganiza sus trenes para septiembre y ya no figuran en su web los servicios de media distancia entre A Coruña y Lugo, ni los de Ourense desde mediados de mes.

La cuenta atrás deja también en el aire el futuro de la actual estación, un edificio de 1875 catalogado en el PXOM que se sumaría a otros dos inmuebles de Adif cerrados desde hace décadas: la casa del guarda y la nave de mercancías. La federación vecinal Lucus Augusti propone convertirlo en puerta turística de la ciudad, pero se desconocen los planes de Adif, que ya ha rehabilitado más de 140 estaciones antiguas en toda España.

articles.headline: Flor Rubinos renuncia como pregonera de A Milagrosa en plena polémica por las reinas y damas
articles.subtitle: La concejala de Zona Rural declina el pregón para no alimentar la confrontación política, un día después de que BNG y PSOE censuraran el acto de proclamación y la implicación de una empresa de una asesora del gobierno local.
articles.body:
La concejala de Zona Rural de Lugo, Flor Rubinos, ha renunciado a ser pregonera de las fiestas de A Milagrosa, que se celebrarán del 2 al 7 de septiembre. El gobierno local explicó que la edil quiere alejarse de la polémica y evitar que su persona sea usada en una confrontación política, y la comisión de fiestas eligió como sustitutos a la maestra y escritora Marisol Bravos y al novelista Jordi Cicely.

La renuncia llega después de que el BNG, a través de Rubén Arroxo, denunciara una presunta incompatibilidad: en el cartel figura la empresa Lucus Espectáculos, cuya única titular es asesora de la propia Rubinos. Arroxo anunció que pondrá el caso en conocimiento de los servicios fiscalizadores del Concello. Tanto él como el PSOE —con Ana González Abelleira al frente— criticaron además la recuperación del acto de proclamación de reinas y damas, pese al acuerdo plenario unánime de 2016 que insta a no dar cobertura a este tipo de actos.

Las asociaciones Agra dos Castros y la Plataforma Feminista de Lugo tacharon el certamen de "anacrónico" y "machista", mientras la comisión aclara que no es un concurso de belleza: serán dos niñas y un niño de cinco años quienes entreguen una flor a las autoridades en la apertura del 4 de septiembre. La diputada del BNG Olalla Rodil ha exigido a la Xunta que retire su apoyo al acto amparándose en la Ley de Igualdad de 2023, mientras el Concello recuerda que solo tramitó permisos y que no hay colaboración económica comprometida.

articles.headline: Muere un joven de 27 años tras salirse de la vía con su coche en Sarria
articles.subtitle: El siniestro ocurrió de madrugada en el kilómetro 19 de la LU-546, en las curvas de Balmao, y eleva a una veintena los fallecidos en las carreteras de la provincia en lo que va de 2026, según La Voz de Galicia.
articles.body:
Un joven de 27 años, vecino de Láncara, ha muerto esta madrugada en un accidente de tráfico en Sarria. El 112 recibió el aviso sobre las 3.30 horas: un coche se había salido de la vía en el kilómetro 19 de la LU-546, en la zona de las curvas de Balmao, y había caído por un terraplén. Viajaban dos personas; uno de los ocupantes salió del vehículo por su propio pie y fue atendido con dolor abdominal, mientras el otro quedó atrapado. Los Bomberos de Sarria lo excarcelaron, pero el personal del 061 solo pudo confirmar su muerte. El herido fue trasladado al Hula.

El accidente se produce tras una jornada negra en las carreteras gallegas: dos personas murieron el martes en sendos siniestros en O Porriño y Verín.

Las carreteras de Lugo acumulan ya una veintena de fallecidos en lo que va de 2026, según los recuentos de La Voz de Galicia. El accidente del 6 de agosto en la A-6, con dos muertos, fue uno de los más graves del verano. La red secundaria y las distracciones al volante concentran la mayoría de las víctimas, en la línea de 2025, cuando 26 personas perdieron la vida, el peor dato desde hace décadas en la provincia.

articles.headline: Lugo restablece 9.500 farolas en una noche y quedan unas 700 averiadas tras la tormenta
articles.subtitle: La ciudad recuperó el lunes 211 de los 365 cuadros eléctricos dañados por el temporal del domingo; el edil de Infraestruturas avisa de que en los próximos días pueden aparecer nuevas averías en la red.
articles.body:
El Concello de Lugo restableció en una sola noche 211 de los cuadros eléctricos que dejó averiados la gran tormenta del domingo, la que el personal de Hallman, empresa que mantiene el alumbrado público, define como la que más daños ha causado en años. Este martes funcionaban ya 350 de los 365 cuadros de los que dependen las 17.000 farolas de la ciudad, según informó el edil de Infraestruturas e Mobilidade, Antonio Ameijide. Quedan unos quince con daños graves, en los que en algunos casos habrá que sustituir aparataje, y unas 700 farolas sin luz.

La noche del domingo, la tormenta, corta pero con intensísimo aparato eléctrico, dejó a oscuras tramos de la Ronda da Muralla, de Ramón Ferreiro y el entorno del parque Rosalía de Castro, y llegó a afectar a cerca de la mitad de los equipos. La red semafórica quedó totalmente restablecida antes del mediodía del lunes.

El gobierno local pide tranquilidad: la reparación total puede tardar días, no solo por la mano de obra necesaria sino por la disponibilidad de repuestos. Además, los técnicos no descartan que en los próximos días surjan nuevas incidencias derivadas del mismo temporal.

articles.headline: Sánchez comparecerá el 3 de septiembre por Ceuta en pleno choque entre Robles y Marlaska por el CNI
articles.subtitle: El Congreso adelanta al próximo miércoles la sesión monográfica sobre la crisis migratoria, mientras el PSOE intenta rebajar la disputa entre Defensa e Interior sobre si los servicios secretos alertaron de la entrada masiva.
articles.body:
Pedro Sánchez comparecerá el próximo 3 de septiembre en un pleno extraordinario del Congreso para dar explicaciones sobre la crisis de Ceuta. El Gobierno pretendía situar la sesión en el primer pleno ordinario, el 9 de septiembre, pero la presión del PP y de Vox, apoyada por la mayoría de los socios parlamentarios, forzó el adelanto. La Diputación Permanente, reunida este miércoles, ratificó la fecha y rechazó por 34 votos frente a 35 las comparecencias urgentes que pedía la oposición para cuatro ministros.

La sesión se celebrará un mes y medio después del asalto a la valla y de la entrada masiva del 30 de julio, en la que, según los recuentos citados en el Congreso, llegaron a contabilizarse hasta 80.000 personas y 140 muertes. En el debate, la portavoz del PP, Ester Muñoz, calificó lo ocurrido como "el mayor fracaso de esta democracia", mientras el PSOE defendió la gestión del Ejecutivo.

## El cruce por los avisos del CNI

La jornada estuvo marcada además por el choque entre los ministerios de Defensa e Interior. Margarita Robles detalló que el CNI alertó de la entrada masiva un día antes, mientras Interior niega haber recibido esa comunicación y Fernando Grande-Marlaska cuenta con el respaldo del ministro Jorge Torres, que aseguró que "no hubo comunicación del CNI". El portavoz socialista, Patxi López, intentó rebajar la polémica: "Las dos versiones pueden ser verdad a la vez", dijo, al considerar posible que el centro de inteligencia avisara de movimientos de personas sin calibrar su dimensión extraordinaria.

articles.headline: La Alhambra reabre el 95% de los Palacios Nazaríes y todo el Generalife tras ocho días de cierre
articles.subtitle: El descenso de la actividad sísmica permite recuperar este miércoles la mayor parte de los recorridos del monumento, aunque la Alcazaba y la Sala del Trono seguirán cerradas por prudencia hasta nuevo aviso.
articles.body:
La Alhambra de Granada reabre este miércoles la mayor parte de sus recorridos, ocho días después del cierre total decretado el 18 de agosto, cuando un terremoto de magnitud 4,8 obligó a evacuar el monumento. El Patronato confirmó que "el descenso sostenido de la actividad sísmica" permite la reapertura completa del Generalife y del 95% de los Palacios Nazaríes, con espacios como el Partal, el Paseo de las Torres y la Sala de la Barca de nuevo accesibles.

Si la tendencia se mantiene, este jueves se incorporarán la Sala de Dos Hermanas, las Habitaciones del Emperador, el Patio de la Reja y el Patio de Lindaraja. La Alcazaba y la Sala del Trono del Palacio de Comares permanecerán cerradas "como medida de prudencia", aunque el Patronato descarta daños estructurales significativos. El horario de visita se mantiene de 8.30 a 20.00 horas.

## La serie sísmica no ha terminado

La actividad comenzó el 14 de agosto y tuvo sus picos con dos terremotos de 4,8, registrados los días 15 y 18. Este martes se contabilizaron 48 temblores en Granada y su área metropolitana, todos por debajo de magnitud 2 y solo dos percibidos por la población, según el Instituto Geográfico Nacional. La serie ha dejado grietas, desprendimientos de cornisas, heridos leves y vecinos desalojados en municipios como Alhendín, Gójar, Ogíjares o La Zubia. El vicepresidente primero, Carlos Cuerpo, visita este miércoles Granada para reunirse con los alcaldes de las localidades afectadas y con la asociación de vecinos del Zaidín.

articles.headline: Unos cohetes explotan entre la multitud en el chupinazo de Noáin: cerca de medio centenar de heridos
articles.subtitle: Las chispas de los dos primeros cohetes prendieron las mechas de los siguientes, que se dispararon hacia abajo y estallaron entre el público congregado en la plaza de los Fueros al mediodía de este miércoles.
articles.body:
Cerca de medio centenar de personas resultaron heridas este miércoles al explotar material pirotécnico en el inicio de las fiestas patronales de Noáin (Navarra). Los hechos ocurrieron sobre las 12.00 horas en la plaza de los Fueros, durante el chupinazo que se lanza desde el balcón del Ayuntamiento. Según Diario de Navarra, las mechas de los cohetes que iban a lanzarse a continuación prendieron con las chispas de los dos primeros, y tres de ellos se dispararon hacia abajo, estallando entre la multitud.

Tres hombres, de 53, 54 y 41 años, fueron trasladados al Hospital Universitario de Navarra por quemaduras y están en proceso de valoración. El resto presenta heridas leves —dolores de oído, quemaduras y lesiones menores— y acudieron por sus propios medios al centro de salud, según el 112. Las cifras varían ligeramente según la fuente: El País habla de en torno a 50 afectados y 20minutos de 47.

La Guardia Civil se ha hecho cargo de la investigación. La presidenta de Navarra, María Chivite, ofreció al alcalde de Noáin la colaboración del Ejecutivo foral y deseó el "pronto restablecimiento" de los heridos. Las imágenes difundidas por Diario de Navarra muestran el caos en la plaza en los instantes posteriores a la explosión.

articles.headline: Una masa de aire polar desploma los termómetros desde el jueves, tras un fin de semana de lluvias con dos muertas en Tarragona
articles.subtitle: Un centro de bajas presiones al noroeste de la Península traerá un descenso térmico casi generalizado y lluvias intensas en Galicia, donde se podrían acumular hasta 150 litros por metro cuadrado en puntos de A Coruña y Pontevedra.
articles.body:
Los meteorólogos anuncian un cambio "importante" de tiempo a partir del jueves, con la llegada de una masa de aire polar que provocará un descenso térmico casi generalizado, impropio de finales de agosto. Según Meteored, un centro de bajas presiones situado al noroeste peninsular favorecerá la llegada de varios frentes: Madrid no superará los 25 grados el jueves, Albacete pasará de 34 a 28 y Murcia caerá desde los 36-37 previstos para este jueves hasta unos 27 el viernes.

La Agencia Estatal de Meteorología mantiene avisos por lluvia y tormentas en el norte, con nivel naranja en el oeste de A Coruña y acumulaciones de hasta 150 litros por metro cuadrado en puntos de Galicia, especialmente en los extremos occidentales de A Coruña y Pontevedra. El frente no llegará al Mediterráneo, donde seguirá el calor con polvo sahariano en Baleares y el sureste, y el riesgo de incendios empeora en la franja central-oriental.

## La factura del temporal anterior

La nueva borrasca llega después de un fin de semana de fuertes lluvias que dejó dos víctimas mortales: una madre y su hija de 18 años, que resultaron heridas el sábado al caer sobre ellas un muro del puerto deportivo de Roda de Berà (Tarragona) y fallecieron el martes por la noche. El Ayuntamiento ha decretado dos días de luto y convocado un minuto de silencio este miércoles a las 19.00 horas.

articles.headline: Secretary of State admits Derry is 'left out of the equation' as Eastwood demands student rebalance
articles.subtitle: Chris Bryant made the admission during his first visit to Derry since becoming Northern Ireland Secretary, prompting SDLP MP Colum Eastwood to press the Executive to rebalance student numbers from Belfast to the North West.
articles.body:
Secretary of State Chris Bryant has acknowledged that the North West "just gets a little bit left out of the equation" during his first visit to Derry, flanked by the new Parliamentary Under-Secretary for Northern Ireland, Sarah Owen.

Speaking to the press at the Factory Girls sculpture beside the Guildhall, Bryant also appeared to criticise the Stormont Executive, saying Northern Ireland needs "a fully functioning political system with collective responsibility; a budget being set by the Executive; and power-sharing really functioning for the people of Northern Ireland". He said it was "crazy" that there is still no budget this financial year and insisted he was "very serious" about the Executive raising its own revenue.

SDLP Foyle MP Colum Eastwood seized on the admission, calling it "indefensible that Belfast currently has nearly 60,000 students, while Derry has just 6,500". He urged the Executive to "force the universities here to rebalance student numbers", saying the parties running it had made promises on Ulster University's Magee expansion that were "rolled back on almost as soon as they were announced", and must deliver "at least 10,000 students" in the city.

Asked about a proposed Executive Office North West office modelled on Number 10 North, Bryant said he was "not sure whether that precise idea is exactly the way we need to go because just having an office doesn't necessarily transform things", echoing Andy Burnham's pledge of "prosperity in every postcode".

On legacy, the Secretary of State said the most important thing was to "get answers for people", while community leaders at the Holywell Trust warned of "decades of under investment in the north west" and urged urgent action on legacy cases.

articles.headline: High Court quashes Drumcree parade restriction as O'Neill warns unionism is moving to 'a more extreme element'
articles.subtitle: The Parades Commission conceded a procedural error after an Orangeman challenged its decision to keep the July parade off Portadown's Garvaghy Road, a route it has been denied since 1998.
articles.body:
The High Court has quashed the Parades Commission's decision to restrict the annual Orange Order parade at Drumcree, after the commission conceded it had not considered the determination in its "final form" - all six members had not signed off on it before it was issued.

The ruling follows a legal challenge by a Portadown Orangeman. The commission has banned the parade from the mainly nationalist Garvaghy Road every year since 1998, when its refusal triggered some of the worst disorder in Northern Ireland's history, including the Ballymoney arson attack that killed the three Quinn children. Any future parade on the road would need a fresh application.

First Minister Michelle O'Neill visited Garvaghy Road residents on Wednesday, accusing unionist leaders of "triumphalism" and of "harking for the days of the past". "That does beg the question, why is unionism limping ever more, or day by day, to the more extreme element of things in society?" she said.

DUP leader Gavin Robinson hit back, saying it was "not triumphalist to expect that applications made to the Parades Commission should be considered properly", while DUP MP Carla Lockhart said she was "dumbfounded" that commissioners had not already resigned. Communities Minister Gordon Lyons claimed the commission made decisions "by WhatsApp" and said confidence in it had collapsed.

Garvaghy Road Residents' Coalition spokesman Breandán Mac Cionnaith was emphatic: "No more marches." The Northern Ireland Office said Sir Chris Bryant would meet the commission's chair "as a priority".

articles.headline: Dáithí Mac Gabhann back home in Belfast after life-changing heart transplant
articles.subtitle: The nine-year-old, whose family's campaign led to Northern Ireland's opt-out organ donation law, spent his first night at home after an eight-year wait for a new heart.
articles.body:
Dáithí Mac Gabhann, the nine-year-old who inspired changes to Northern Ireland's organ donation laws, has spent his first night at home in west Belfast after receiving a heart transplant following an eight-year wait.

Dáithí was born in 2016 with hypoplastic left heart syndrome, meaning the left side of his heart did not form correctly, and had been on the transplant waiting list since 2018. The operation was carried out last month at the Freeman Hospital in Newcastle upon Tyne.

Friends and neighbours cheered as he returned home after several weeks in England. His father, Máirtín, said it was "absolutely incredible seeing everybody here today to welcome Dáithí home", and paid tribute to the donor family: "They've saved so much more than Dáithí, they've saved our whole family, our friends and the whole community around us."

His family campaigned for years for a soft opt-out organ donation system, and Dáithí's Law came into effect in June 2023. Irish President Catherine Connolly said she was "overjoyed at the wonderful news", while First Minister Michelle O'Neill said there was "no stronger wee boy" and congratulated the family.

Dáithí, who arrived home in his beloved Liverpool colours, is expected to return to school on 1 October.

articles.headline: Four men charged over replica mosque hate display on Moygashel bonfire
articles.subtitle: Three men face charges of displaying written material to stir up hatred, while a 74-year-old was charged with intimidation over the July bonfire in Co Tyrone that provoked widespread condemnation.
articles.body:
Four men have been charged in connection with a hate display placed on a loyalist bonfire in Moygashel, on the outskirts of Dungannon, in July.

Three of the men, aged 28, 38 and 58, were charged with displaying written material to stir up hatred or arouse fear, while a 74-year-old man was charged with intimidation. All four are due to appear before Dungannon Magistrates' Court on 16 September.

The charges follow the arrests on Tuesday of five men - aged 27, 38, 51, 58 and 74 - by detectives in mid-Ulster on suspicion of offences under the Public Order Act, with a 51-year-old subsequently released.

The bonfire had been topped with a replica of a mosque and signs reading "secure our borders" and "end the threat of radical Islam", provoking revulsion and condemnation from political parties, religious leaders and human rights groups. The PSNI had planned to remove the structure, but it was ignited before officers had the chance.

District Commander Superintendent Peter Stevenson said the investigation into the placing of offensive materials on the bonfire continues. One man was previously arrested in the same investigation in July and has appeared in court. Last year, a bonfire at the same spot was topped with an effigy of migrants in a boat, which the PSNI investigated as a hate incident.

articles.headline: Date set for £100 home heating oil voucher scheme for 340,000 NI households
articles.subtitle: Applications for the Home Heating Oil Support Scheme open on 9 September, offering a £100 voucher to low-income households that rely on oil for heating, with the scheme running until March 2027.
articles.body:
The £100 Home Heating Oil Support Scheme for Northern Ireland will open for applications on 9 September, Communities Minister Gordon Lyons has announced.

Around 340,000 lower-income households are expected to qualify for the one-off payment, funded by £17.2 million from the UK Government plus £19.2 million added by the Executive. One voucher will be available per qualifying address.

To be eligible, households must use oil as their main source of heating for at least one day in either April or November 2026, and either receive a qualifying benefit - including Pension Credit, Universal Credit and disability benefits - or have a combined annual income of less than £30,000 after allowable deductions.

Applications will be made online through nidirect, with help available at Jobs and Benefits offices and on a dedicated helpline. Successful applicants will receive a payment card usable only at participating oil suppliers, within up to 10 working days, with around three-quarters of applications processed automatically. The scheme closes on 31 March 2027.

Around two thirds of Northern Ireland households use home heating oil, by far the highest proportion of any UK region, and prices remain roughly 50% higher than before the Iran conflict, despite falling back from their peak.

Lyons said his officials had "worked at pace to put in place a fair and robust system", while separately, Economy Minister Dr Caoimhe Archibald said a single combined electricity payment of over £50 for all households is anticipated to be paid from October.

articles.headline: Flash flood on Nepal-Tibet border leaves scores dead and hundreds missing
articles.subtitle: A wall of water hit the Bhote Koshi river valley in Rasuwa district early Wednesday after an earthquake-triggered avalanche, washing away villages, bridges and roads and leaving hundreds of tourists and residents unaccounted for.
articles.body:
At least 95 people have been confirmed dead and hundreds more are missing after a flash flood and mudslide along the Nepal-Tibet border swept through riverside settlements in northern Nepal on Wednesday, with the toll expected to rise as waters recede.

The flood hit in Rasuwa district, just north of Kathmandu, early on Wednesday. Initial assessments point to an earthquake at around 8.37am triggering an avalanche and landslide that blocked the Bhote Koshi river before bursting, sending a wall of mud and water downstream. Three people were killed in Tibet, where 265 others are missing.

Villages including Timure and Syabrubesi were badly damaged, along with the Timure customs office area. Verified footage showed the flood ripping a bridge from its supports at Trishuli Bazaar in Nuwakot district, about 25km from Kathmandu, before multi-storey buildings collapsed into the torrent.

Nepal's tourism authority said work was under way to establish the whereabouts of hundreds of travellers - the Reuters news agency reported that at least 384 people, including 105 Indians, 93 Nepalis, 12 British nationals and three US citizens, were missing in the region. Nepal's foreign minister told parliament that dozens of police, armed police and soldiers were also unaccounted for.

Rescue helicopters struggled to land in the mountainous terrain, and the main road to Kathmandu was closed. Authorities warned that a blockage still lodged upstream could trigger a second flood, and urged residents along the Trishuli river corridor to remain on high alert.

articles.headline: Haiti gang attack kills 47 and kidnaps more than 50 near Port-au-Prince
articles.subtitle: The Sunday raid on the hillside community of Kenscoff is believed to be one of the largest mass kidnappings in Haiti in recent years, with a gang leader threatening to kill hostages if authorities act.
articles.body:
At least 47 people were killed and more than 50 others kidnapped when armed men attacked the once-peaceful community of Kenscoff, in the hills above Port-au-Prince, the United Nations said Tuesday, in one of the largest mass kidnappings Haiti has seen in years.

At least five of those killed were children, according to the UN Integrated Office in Haiti (BINUH), which said 22 of the victims were reportedly executed after seeking shelter. UN Secretary General António Guterres condemned the attack, saying it underscored the "alarming security conditions" in the country.

Kenscoff mayor Jean Massillon told the Associated Press that gang members set fire to 25 homes and killed two government employees, including his cousin, who served as his security detail. A gang leader has threatened to kill the hostages if authorities kill any gang members while trying to secure the community.

Sunday's attack pierced growing hopes that security was improving in the troubled Caribbean nation. The first major attack on Kenscoff came in January 2025, since when gangs have carried out sporadic raids on the mountains surrounding the capital, displacing thousands.

Gang violence has now displaced a record 1.5 million people across Haiti, where more than 3,050 people were reported killed between January and June this year, according to UN statistics. Armed groups are estimated to control around 70% of Port-au-Prince.

articles.headline: Fourteen newborn babies die in fire at Islamabad hospital maternity ward
articles.subtitle: The blaze broke out in an air-conditioning unit at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences early Wednesday, and witnesses say the ward's locked door delayed the rescue; the PM has suspended a top health official.
articles.body:
At least 14 newborn babies have died in a fire that broke out before dawn on Wednesday in the maternity ward of the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS), the biggest state hospital in Islamabad.

The blaze started in an air-conditioning unit on the third floor of the mother and child ward and was quickly fuelled by oxygen connections. Of the 15 babies in the intensive care unit at the time, only one was saved; seven other babies, two men and 10 mothers were also rescued, according to Pakistan's minister of state for interior.

Witnesses told the AFP news agency that the door to the maternity ward was locked, and that people had to "break the door down" while rescue teams smashed windows to fight the flames. One father said the building "had no fire security, no proper exits. All doors were closed." The hospital's executive director denied the door was locked, saying it was manned to protect babies from being stolen.

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has suspended Federal Secretary of Health Aslam Ghauri, and ordered an immediate investigation. Police said the newborns were so severely burned that DNA testing will be needed to confirm their identities before their bodies are released to families.

Fires in large buildings are frequent in Pakistan, often blamed on poor safety regulations and lax enforcement of building codes.

articles.headline: Canada announces 'dollar-for-dollar' retaliatory tariffs on US as high as 50%
articles.subtitle: Ottawa's response to Washington's new levies has sent toilet paper prices surging in the US, with the escalating trade war now hitting American store shelves.
articles.body:
Canada has announced "dollar-for-dollar" retaliatory tariffs on US goods, reaching as high as 50%, in an escalation of the trade war between the two countries that is now being felt on American supermarket shelves.

The announcement follows Washington's latest round of levies on Canadian imports, and comes amid reports of surging toilet paper prices across the United States. Analysts say the paper-product crunch is a direct consequence of the cross-border tariff dispute, which has disrupted supply chains for a category in which Canada is a major producer.

The escalation is the latest twist in a confrontation that has seen tariffs paused, reinstated and expanded over recent weeks. It also threatens to upend the economic picture in both countries, with Canada warning of significant impacts on US consumers and businesses.

The dispute has become a defining test of the limits of American economic power under the Trump administration, with Ottawa vowing to respond proportionately to every tariff Washington imposes. Both governments have signalled willingness to negotiate, but no new talks have been announced.

articles.headline: Apple debuts M6, its first 2nm chip, and the quad-die M5 Ultra in new Mac mini and Mac Studio
articles.subtitle: The M6 lands in the Mac mini with the world's fastest CPU core and a Dual 16-core Neural Engine, while the M5 Ultra fuses four dies to power up to 512GB of unified memory for on-device AI.
articles.body:
Apple has unveiled two new desktop chips: the M6, its first processor built on a 2-nanometer process, and the M5 Ultra, the most powerful M-series chip yet, debuting in the new Mac mini and Mac Studio.

The M6 advances every compute block, with a larger 12-core CPU featuring what Apple calls the world's fastest CPU core, a 12-core GPU with Neural Accelerators, a Dual 16-core Neural Engine rated at up to twice the AI compute of previous generations, and up to 170GB/s of unified memory bandwidth. Apple said the M6 delivers "a revolutionary leap in everyday performance and power efficiency."

The M5 Ultra uses next-generation UltraFusion technology to join two dual-die M5 Max chips into a quad-die architecture - a first for Apple silicon - with over 4.4TB/s of inter-die bandwidth. It scales to a 36-core CPU, an 80-core GPU with Neural Accelerators, and a massive 512GB unified memory pool with 1.2TB/s of bandwidth, 50% more than the M3 Ultra. Apple says the M5 Ultra delivers up to 4.3x the peak AI compute of the M3 Ultra, letting pros run frontier-class models entirely on device.

Mac Studio starts at $2,499 with M5 Max and $5,499 with M5 Ultra, while the Mac mini opens at $899 with the M6. Both machines add Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6, pre-orders are open, and deliveries begin September 22. The launch also reflects a broader trend: Mac prices now start at raised levels set during the global memory shortage that has gripped the industry since late 2025.

articles.headline: Meta to pay up to $16.7 billion to settle social media harms case with 29 US states
articles.subtitle: The deal resolves state lawsuits alleging Instagram and Facebook addict children and teens, and comes as lawmakers push for sweeping federal online safety legislation.
articles.body:
Meta has agreed to pay up to $16.7 billion to settle a lawsuit brought by 29 US states over social media harms to children and teenagers, one of the largest state-level settlements in US history.

The lawsuit, filed by a bipartisan coalition of state attorneys general, alleged that Meta's Instagram and Facebook platforms were designed to addict minors, with the company repeatedly ignoring evidence of psychological harm. TechCrunch reported the settlement at $18 billion, while Wired and Hacker News pegged the headline figure at up to $16.7 billion, with the deal covering both monetary relief and changes to product practices.

Under the terms, Meta will fund youth mental health programs and make platform changes, including default privacy settings and time-management tools for minors. The settlement does not include an admission of liability.

The agreement follows a landmark jury verdict earlier this month in a separate federal case that found social media companies liable for addicting young users, and arrives as Congress weighs a federal kids' online safety bill that would impose new obligations on platforms nationwide. Meta said it remains committed to working with states and regulators, while critics argue the settlement lets the company off the hook for systemic design choices.

articles.headline: AWS acquires DuckLabs, the company behind open source database DuckDB
articles.subtitle: The Amsterdam-based team behind the hugely popular embedded analytics database will join AWS, while DuckDB itself remains free and open source under the independent DuckDB Foundation.
articles.body:
Amazon Web Services has signed a definitive agreement to acquire DuckLabs, the Amsterdam-based company behind DuckDB, the open source analytical database that has become a darling of developers worldwide.

Financial terms were not disclosed. The transaction is expected to close in early September, after which DuckLabs' team of more than 30 engineers will join AWS, remaining in Amsterdam. Founders Hannes Mühleisen and Mark Raasveldt will continue to lead the team and the open source project's technical direction.

Crucially, AWS said it is not acquiring the DuckDB open source project itself: DuckDB, DuckLake and Quack will remain free and open source under their MIT licenses, stewarded by the non-profit DuckDB Foundation. AWS's Andy Warfield said the company is "committed to the project's continued development in open source."

The deal deepens a collaboration that began in early 2025, when the two teams worked together on DuckDB support for Amazon S3 Tables and SageMaker Lakehouse. DuckDB now sees more than three million downloads per day, and the acquisition gives AWS a marquee embeddable analytics engine as it competes with rivals on data workloads.

DuckLabs said joining AWS means it will no longer depend on converting free users into commercial support customers, and plans to expand the DuckDB Foundation's role, including an advisory board through which commercial users can shape the project roadmap.

articles.headline: Anthropic unifies Claude's memory across chat and Cowork, with sensitive topics excluded by default
articles.subtitle: The update lets users see everything Claude remembers topic by topic, edit or delete any of it, and keeps health, beliefs and similar subjects out of memory unless explicitly enabled.
articles.body:
Anthropic has overhauled how its Claude AI assistant remembers users, unifying memory across its chat interface and Claude Cowork, its agentic desktop product, so that context built up in one surface now carries over to the other automatically.

"The memory you use in chat is the same as in Claude Cowork. Now, wherever you work with Claude, it starts from what it already knows about you," the company announced on Monday.

Claude now adds topics to memory as conversations happen rather than summarizing sessions after they end - mention that a project deadline moved to September, and the next conversation already knows. Everything Claude remembers is listed as short files under Topics in Memory settings, where users can read, edit or delete each one; correcting a company's old name in one file fixes it everywhere.

Sensitive subjects are handled separately and are off by default across all tiers. Claude does not store health, race, ethnicity, religion, politics or gender identity unless a user flips a toggle, and certain categories - government ID numbers, criminal history, immigration status - are never saved, even when sensitive topics are enabled.

Memory is on by default for Free, Pro and Max plans on web, desktop and mobile, and can be paused or reset at any time. Team and Enterprise admins control availability, with memory off by default for individual users in those plans. The change is a product and settings update rather than a new model release, and Anthropic noted that Claude Code is not part of the unified memory system.

articles.headline: Z.ai reveals it is the lab behind the mysterious Ox Alpha model - and will release its weights
articles.subtitle: The stealth model that rivals DeepSeek is confirmed as part of the GLM series from the Chinese AI lab, which says open weights are on the way.
articles.body:
The mystery behind Ox Alpha, a stealth AI model that has been turning heads in the developer community, is over: it is the work of Z.ai, the Chinese lab behind the GLM family of open source models.

The reveal was reported by TechCrunch and Bloomberg, which noted that Ox Alpha has been quietly rivaling DeepSeek in benchmarks and developer buzz. Z.ai has now confirmed that Ox Alpha is a new GLM-series model and that it will release its weights, a decision consistent with the lab's history of open sourcing its models.

The confirmation arrived as Z.ai also shipped GLM-5.3-Flash, the latest addition to the GLM lineup, and follows the wider pattern of Chinese labs pushing open-weight frontier-class models. Ox Alpha's capabilities had sparked speculation across Hacker News and AI circles since it appeared, with observers comparing its performance and efficiency to DeepSeek's most recent releases.

Z.ai, backed by the same group that founded the large language model startup Zhipu AI, has positioned open weights as central to its strategy. Developers will be watching whether Ox Alpha's release lives up to the hype and how it reshapes the competitive landscape of open and closed frontier models.
